To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
crowds provide valid eval-uations if the crowd is large enough or the crowd is highly expert.
the evaluation of ideas is valid when the crowd is big and the evaluation of concepts and solution is valid when the expertise of the crowd is high.

crowds provide valid evalua-tions when 1) the number of individuals within the crowds is high, 2) the time to outcome/verification of evaluation is low, 3) the degree of expertise of individuals within the crow is high, 4) the degree of strategic importance of the evaluation challenge is high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how crowds can be used to evaluate new ideas, concepts, or problem solutions.
the question of whether crowds can provide valid evaluations for ideas, concepts, or problem solu-tions in different phases of development.
the validity of crowds as an evaluation method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the validity of crowds is dependent on the evaluation task and the type of crowd used for it.

the validity of crowd evaluations is higher than the validity of evaluations of experts in the case that crowds are used to evaluate ideas in NPD and in the case of solutions in the context of open inno-va-tion and user innovation.
crowds are a valid alternative to experts for evaluations in idea, con-cept and solution development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
com-panies can use the wisdom of the crowd to evaluate ideas, concepts, or solutions in a valid way.
crowds can provide valid evaluations for ideas, concepts, or solutions in the early stages of development, whereas the evaluation of solutions in the later stages should be done by experts.
the validity of crowdsourcing evaluations depends on the type and the phase of evaluation challenge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crowds can be used to evaluate ideas, concepts, or solutions in different stages of development.
companies should not only focus on the number of ideas but also on the expertise of crowds to achieve valid evaluations.
the validity of evaluations can be influenced by the crowd size and expertise of the evaluators, but also by the strategic importance, the time to outcome, and the number of ideas to evaluate.
